{{神社| 名称=志紀県主神社| 所在地=大阪府藤井寺市惣社1-6-23| 位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|scale:30000}}| 祭神=神八井耳命| 社格=式内社（大）・河内国総社・村社| 例祭=[[10月9日]]}}
'''志紀県主神社'''（しきあがたぬしじんじゃ）は、[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]にある[[神社]]である。[[式内社]]、[[河内国]][[総社]]で、旧[[社格]]は[[村社]]。
==祭神== [[神武天皇]]の長子である[[神八井耳命]]を主[[祭神]]とし、伊勢大神（[[天照大神]]）・[[春日神|春日大神]]（[[天児屋命]]・[[比売神|比咩大神]]・[[タケミカヅチ|武甕槌命]]・[[経津主神|経津主命]]）・[[住吉三神|住吉三柱神]]・[[神功皇后]]を配祀する。ただし、『河内名所図会』では祭神を「磯城県主黒速」としている。
==歴史== [[奈良時代]]、この一帯は「志貴（磯城）の県」という朝廷の直轄地で、それを管理していたのは神八井耳命を祖とする志貴県主（しきのあがたぬし）と、その同族の志貴首（しきのおびと）であった。創建の由緒は不詳であるが、当社はその氏神として創建されたものとみられ、『河内誌』に「国府属邑一」とあることから、この地に河内[[国府]]が設置されたときに創建されたものと考えられている。河内国の総社とされ、[[延喜式神名帳]]では大社に列している。
中世には、[[楠木正成]]が[[祈願所]]としてに隆昌を極めたが、[[楠木氏]]の衰亡とともに衰退し、さらに戦国時代にはたびたび兵火にかかり、何度か遷座を余儀なくされた。
明治5年村社に列した。

鳥居と拝殿| 例祭=[[10月9日]]}} '''志貴県主神社'''（しきあがたぬしじんじゃ）は、[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]にある[[神社]]である。[[式内社]]、[[河内国]][[総社]]で、旧[[社格]]は[[村社]]。 ==祭神== [[神武天皇]]の長子である[[神八井耳命]]を主[[祭神]]とし、伊勢大神（[[天照大神]]）・[[春日神|春日大神]]（[[天児屋命]]・[[比売神|比咩大神]]・[[タケミカヅチ|武甕槌命]]・[[経津主神|経津主命]]）・[[住吉三神|住吉三柱神]]・[[神功皇后]]を配祀する。ただし、『河内名所図会』では祭神を「磯城県主黒速」としている。 ==歴史== [[奈良時代]]、この一帯は「志貴（磯城）の県」という朝廷の直轄地で、それを管理していたのは神八井耳命を祖とする志貴県主（しきのあがたぬし）と、その同族の志貴首（しきのおびと）であった。創建の由緒は不詳であるが、当社はその氏神として創建されたものとみられ、『河内誌』に「国府属邑一」とあることから、この地に河内[[国府]]が設置されたときに創建されたものと考えられている。河内国の総社とされ、[[延喜式神名帳]]では大社に列している。 中世には、[[楠木正成]]が[[祈願所]]としてに隆昌を極めたが、[[楠木氏]]の衰亡とともに衰退し、さらに戦国時代にはたびたび兵火にかかり、何度か遷座を余儀なくされた。 明治5年村社に列した。 {{DEFAULTSORT:しきあかたぬししんしや}} [[Category:大阪府の神社]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:河内国の式内社|大しきあかたぬししんしや]] [[Category:大阪府の旧村社]] [[Category:藤井寺市]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:河内国|社0]] {{shinto-stub}}

旧[[村社]] |創建=不詳 |本殿= |別名= 総社（通称） |札所等= |例祭= [[10月9日]] |神事= }} '''志貴県主神社'''（しきあがたぬしじんじゃ）は、[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]にある[[神社]]である。[[式内社]]、[[河内国]][[総社]]で、旧[[社格]]は[[村社]]。 ==祭神== ; 主祭神 * [[神八井耳命]] - [[神武天皇]]の長子である ; 配祀神 * 伊勢大神（[[天照大神]]） * [[春日神|春日大神]]（[[天児屋命]]・[[比売神|比咩大神]]・[[タケミカヅチ|武甕槌命]]・[[経津主神|経津主命]]） * [[住吉三神|住吉三柱神]] * [[神功皇后]] ただし、『河内名所図会』では祭神を「磯城県主[[弟磯城|黒速]]」としている。 ==歴史== [[奈良時代]]、この一帯は「志貴（磯城）の県」という朝廷の直轄地で、それを管理していたのは神八井耳命を祖とする志貴県主（しきのあがたぬし）と、その同族の志貴首（しきのおびと）であった。創建の由緒は不詳であるが、当社はその氏神として創建されたものとみられ、『河内誌』に「国府属邑一」とあることから、この地に河内[[国府]]が設置されたときに創建されたものと考えられている。河内国の総社とされ、[[延喜式神名帳]]では大社に列している。 中世には、[[楠木正成]]が[[祈願所]]としてに隆昌を極めたが、[[楠木氏]]の衰亡とともに衰退し、さらに戦国時代にはたびたび兵火にかかり、何度か遷座を余儀なくされた。明治5年村社に列した。 == 境内 == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|本殿と境内社 File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|境内の河内国府址碑 File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|鳥居 == 現地情報 == ;所在地 *[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]惣社1-6-23 ;交通アクセス * 最寄駅：[[近鉄南大阪線]][[土師ノ里駅]]下車後、徒歩約12分（北東へ約1000m） ==外部リンク== {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} *[http://www.jinjacho-osaka.net/osakafunai-no-jinjya/dai11sibu/fujiidera-city/m27_10_fujiidera_sikiagatanusi.html 志貴県主神社 - 大阪府神社庁] {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:しきあかたぬししんしや}} [[Category:大阪府の神社]] [[Category:藤井寺市の建築物]] [[Category:藤井寺市の歴史]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:河内国の式内社|大しきあかたぬししんしや]] [[Category:大阪府の旧村社]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:河内国|社0]]

{{Shrine |image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |address = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|en|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] }} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as a {{ill|Mura-sha|en|村社}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|en|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|en|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|en|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|en|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|en|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|en|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] }} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as a {{ill|Mura-sha|en|村社}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|en|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|en|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|en|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|en|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|en|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated a {{ill|Mura-sha|en|村社}} in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] }} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * [https://www.osaka-jinjacho.jp/funai_jinja/dai11shibu/fujiidera-city/11048shikiagatanushijinja.html Shiki Agatanushi Shrine - Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] (Japanese) {{Shinto Sidebar}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} [[Category:Pages that were the oldest for a long time so I am {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] }} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] }} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * [https://www.osaka-jinjacho.jp/funai_jinja/dai11shibu/fujiidera-city/11048shikiagatanushijinja.html Shiki Agatanushi Shrine - Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] (Japanese) {{Shinto}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} [[Category:new pages]][[Category:Pages that were the oldest for a long time Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * [https://www.osaka-jinjacho.jp/funai_jinja/dai11shibu/fujiidera-city/11048shikiagatanushijinja.html Shiki Agatanushi Shrine - Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] (Japanese) {{Shinto}} Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds ==
