Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * [https://www.osaka-jinjacho.jp/funai_jinja/dai11shibu/fujiidera-city/11048shikiagatanushijinja.html Shiki Agatanushi Shrine - Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] (Japanese) {{Shinto}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds ==
