{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en}}. == Grounds == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = [[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. Worship Hall |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|34|34|35|N|135|37|06|E|region:JP|name=Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=draft}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社|12=draft}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[October 9]] |type=unranked shrine}} '''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} of major rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=draft}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=draft}}. == Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. ; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=draft}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=draft}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=draft}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en}} deities * [[Empress Jingū]] However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=draft}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=draft}}." == History == In the [[Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=draft}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=draft}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=draft}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=draft}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=draft}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=draft}}. Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=draft}}. == Grounds == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate == Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan ; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en|12=draft}}. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * [https://www.osaka-jinjacho.jp/funai_jinja/dai11shibu/fujiidera-city/11048shikiagatanushijinja.html Shiki Agatanushi Shrine - Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] (Japanese) {{Shinto}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Shikiagatanushi Shrine]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Historical sites in Fujiidera]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Mura-sha]] [[Category:Kawachi Province|Shrine]] [[Category:Buildings in Fujiidera]] [[Category:New]] }} [[sn:Shikiagatanushi Shrine]] [[ja:志貴県主神社]] [[sn:hikiagatanushi Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Shiki Agatanushi Shrine}}

{{神社 |名称=志貴県主神社 |画像=[[File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px]]
拝殿 |所在地=[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]惣社1-6-23 | 緯度度 = 34 | 緯度分 = 34 | 緯度秒 = 35 | N(北緯)及びS(南緯) = N | 経度度 = 135 |経度分 = 37 | 経度秒 = 06 | E(東経)及びW(西経) = E | 地図国コード = JP-27 | 地図 = Japan Osaka | ラベル位置 = left |祭神=[[神八井耳命]] |社格=[[式内社]]（大）
旧[[村社]] |創建=不詳 |本殿= |別名= 総社（通称） |札所等= |例祭= [[10月9日]] |神事= }} '''志貴県主神社'''（しきあがたぬしじんじゃ）は、[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]にある[[神社]]である。[[式内社]]、[[河内国]][[総社]]で、旧[[社格]]は[[村社]]。 ==祭神== ; 主祭神 * [[神八井耳命]] - [[神武天皇]]の長子である ; 配祀神 * 伊勢大神（[[天照大神]]） * [[春日神|春日大神]]（[[天児屋命]]・[[比売神|比咩大神]]・[[タケミカヅチ|武甕槌命]]・[[経津主神|経津主命]]） * [[住吉三神|住吉三柱神]] * [[神功皇后]] ただし、『河内名所図会』では祭神を「磯城県主[[弟磯城|黒速]]」としている。 ==歴史== [[奈良時代]]、この一帯は「志貴（磯城）の県」という朝廷の直轄地で、それを管理していたのは神八井耳命を祖とする志貴[[県主]]（しきのあがたぬし）と、その同族の志貴首（しきのおびと）であった。創建の由緒は不詳であるが、当社はその氏神として創建されたものとみられ、『河内誌』に「国府属邑一」とあることから、この地に河内[[国府]]が設置されたときに創建されたものと考えられている。河内国の総社とされ、[[延喜式神名帳]]では大社に列している。 中世には、[[楠木正成]]が[[祈願所]]としてに隆昌を極めたが、[[楠木氏]]の衰亡とともに衰退し、さらに戦国時代にはたびたび兵火にかかり、何度か遷座を余儀なくされた。明治5年村社に列した。当神社の約100メートル北には神八井耳主命のかくれ廟とされ[[天御中主神]]を主祭神とする黒田神社が鎮座する。 == 境内 == File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|本殿と境内社 File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|境内の河内国府址碑 File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|鳥居 == 現地情報 == ;所在地 *[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]惣社1-6-23 ([[市ノ山古墳|允恭天皇陵]]の北) ;交通アクセス * 最寄駅：[[近鉄南大阪線]][[土師ノ里駅]]下車後、徒歩約12分（北東へ約1000m） ==外部リンク== {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} *[https://www.osaka-jinjacho.jp/funai_jinja/dai11shibu/fujiidera-city/11048shikiagatanushijinja.html 志貴県主神社 - 大阪府神社庁] {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:しきあかたぬししんしや}} [[Category:大阪府の神社]] [[Category:藤井寺市の建築物]] [[Category:藤井寺市の歴史]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:河内国の式内社|大しきあかたぬししんしや]] [[Category:大阪府の旧村社]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:河内国|社0]]

The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|qq=}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}. During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
