<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja]][[ja:志貴県主神社]] {{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11491140]] Wikidata name: Shiki agatanushi-jinja [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:18, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{Coord|34.576388888888886|N|135.61833333333334|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mura-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[:en:October 9|October 9]] |type=unranked shrine|location = {{ill|Fujiidera|WD=Q634011}} }}
'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.
== Grounds == <gallery> File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
== Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan
; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hajinosato Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|qq=}}.
== External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * [https://www.osaka-jinjacho.jp/funai_jinja/dai11shibu/fujiidera-city/11048shikiagatanushijinja.html Shiki Agatanushi Shrine - Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] (Japanese)

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja]][[ja:志貴県主神社]] {{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11491140]] Wikidata name: Shiki agatanushi-jinja [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:18, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{Coord|34.576388888888886|N|135.61833333333334|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mura-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[:en:October 9|October 9]] |type=unranked shrine|location = {{ill|Fujiidera|WD=Q634011}} }}
'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.
== Grounds == <gallery> File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
== Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan
; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hajinosato Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|qq=}}.
== External Links == {{Commonscat|Shiki Agatanushi-jinja}} * [https://www.osaka-jinjacho.jp/funai_jinja/dai11shibu/fujiidera-city/11048shikiagatanushijinja.html Shiki Agatanushi Shrine - Osaka Prefecture Shrine Association] (Japanese)

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja]][[ja:志貴県主神社]] {{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11491140]] Wikidata name: Shiki agatanushi-jinja [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:18, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|image = File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, haiden.jpg |name = Shiki Agatanushi Shrine |location = 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{Coord|34.576388888888886|N|135.61833333333334|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (major), former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, former {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mura-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} |establishment = Unknown |main_hall = Unknown |former_name = Sōja (common name) |festivals = [[:en:October 9|October 9]] |type=unranked shrine|location = {{ill|Fujiidera|WD=Q634011}} }}
'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.
== Grounds == <gallery> File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, honden.jpg|main hall and auxiliary shrines File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, sekihi.jpg|Monument marking the site of Kawachi Kokufu File:Shiki Agatanushi-jinja, torii-2.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
== Visitor Information == ; location * 1-6-23 Sōja, Fujiidera City, Osaka Prefecture, Japan
; Access * Approximately 12 minutes' walk (1 km northeast) from {{ill|Hajinosato Station|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hajinosato Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.

'''Shiki Agatanushi Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|志貴県主神社}}, Shiki Agatanushi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Fujiidera, Osaka|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiidera, Osaka|qq=}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of major Rank, the former {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Province|qq=}}, and was formerly classified as an unranked shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.
== Enshrined Deities == ; Primary deity * '''[[Kamuyaimimi|Kamuyaimimi no Mikoto]]''' - Eldest son of [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].
; Additional deities * Ise Ōkami ({{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}) * {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} deities ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=}}, {{ill|Himegami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegami|qq=}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemikazuchi|qq=}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsunushi|qq=}}) * {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi-taisha|qq=}} deities * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]
However, the ''{{ill|Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja|河内名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' lists the deity as "Shiki Agatanushi {{ill|Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja|弟磯城黒速|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomoshiki no Kurohaya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}."
== History == In the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], the area was known as "Shiki no Agata," an imperial domain managed by the {{ill|Shiki Agatanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki Agatanushi|qq=}}, descendants of [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]], and their kin, the {{ill|Shiki no Obito|ja|志貴首|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Obito|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The shrine is thought to have been founded as the tutelary shrine of these clans. ''{{ill|Kawachi-shi|ja|河内誌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi-shi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'' describes it as "one of the villages attached to the provincial capital," suggesting it was established with the founding of the provincial capital ({{ill|Kokufu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu|qq=}}) of Kawachi. The shrine was recognized as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of the province and is listed as a major shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}.
During the medieval period, the shrine thrived as a {{ill|Kigan-sho|ja|祈願所|1=Kigan-sho|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|13=User:Immanuelle/Kigan-sho|qq=}} under the patronage of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki Masashige|qq=}}, but it later declined alongside the fall of the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki clan|qq=}}. The shrine suffered destruction during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and was relocated multiple times. It was designated an unranked shrine in 1873 during the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}.
Approximately 100 meters north of the shrine is the {{ill|Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Black Shrine (Kuroda Shrine)|qq=}}, dedicated to [[Kamuyaimimi|Kamiyaimimi no Mikoto]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Minakanushi|qq=}}.
